Nina (CSM): need a compact customer-facing runbook (1 pager) we can hand to mid-market accounts: actionable preseed/prefill steps, client batching guidance, streaming + slow-path fallback, TTL guidance, circuit breakers, and a short onboarding checklist that ties to renewal-risk signals. keep language simple.
Arjun (SE): drafting bullets. will separate into two columns: 'Redwood-side' and 'Customer-side'.
Arjun (SE): Top summary (3 lines):
Redwood helps keep inference fast and predictable by warming model caches, offering streaming with graceful fallbacks, and providing observability. Follow the checklist to reduce cold-starts, manage costs, and surface renewal risks early. We recommend a short warmup and a minimal telemetry set to monitor health.
Arjun (SE): Redwood-side actions:
- Warm pools: we can pre-allocate warm workers for your tenant for a scheduled window.
- Prefill API: run small synthetic requests to populate KV and tokenizer caches.
- Verified fallback models: automatic switch to a lower-latency variant when latency SLOs are breached.
- Canary rollouts: 1% staged traffic for model updates; automated rollback on errors.
- Alerts: built-in rules for sustained 5xx or p95 latency breaches.
Arjun (SE): Customer-side recommendations:
- Prefill schedule: run prefill 30120 minutes before expected traffic, with ~5 lightweight prompts.
- Client batching: use batch sizes 40 for user-facing low-latency endpoints; larger behind-the-scenes batchers OK.
- Streaming: enable stream=true; set client-side 2s cutoff to show partial content, then fetch full via non-stream if needed.
- Cache TTLs: conversation/session prefix = 450 min, ephemeral result cache = 105 min. Invalidate when you push prompt or model changes.
- Retries & circuit breakers: stop client retries after 3 attempts within 30s; implement exponential backoff. Server breaker trips if 5xx_rate > 1% for 5 minutes.
Priya (CS Ops): onboarding checklist (CS <> customer):
1) Preflight (CS): call /health and run sample generate (3 prompts). capture baseline median_latency_ms and tokens/min.
2) Warmup (CS + customer): schedule a 15m warmup 1h before go-live. run prefill and confirm prefill_success_rate > 95%.
3) Telemetry (customer): share dashboard link; add queries for median_latency, p95_latency, fallback_rate.
4) Escalation (CS): confirm on-call contact and SLOs; set incident play if 5xx_rate > 1% for 5m.
5) Post-launch (CS): check usage delta day 1, 7, 14.
Priya (CS Ops): renewal-risk flags (auto-checks):
- usage_drop_pct > 30% vs prior week after day 14
- prefill_success_rate < 90% during warmup
- sustained fallback_rate increase > 10% over 24h
- customer-reported quality regressions in first 30 days
Leah (AE): include a short note on cost control: prefer quantized variants for bulk batch jobs and set soft limits on tokens/response length per route.
Tom (SRE): ops safety nuggets to show customers (keep short):
- Slow-path fallback: if primary model > 1.5x latency SLO, route to verified low-latency variant.
- Circuit breaker behavior: after breaker trips, queue incoming requests for 30s and reject new ones to prevent cascading.
- Heartbeat probe: run a lightweight probe every 60s to verify warm pool readiness.
Arjun (SE): example client config (customer can paste):
```
{
  "batch_size": 8,
  "stream": true,
  "prefill": { "enabled": true, "window_minutes": 60 },
  "cache_ttl_seconds": 2700,
  "retry_policy": { "max_attempts": 3, "initial_backoff_ms": 200 },
  "fallback_policy": { "enabled": true, "primary_timeout_ms": 1200 }
}
```
Arjun (SE): prefill curl example (one-liner):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/prefill -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"tenant_id":"T-ACME","prompts":["hi","summarize: 1 line","extract key points: short"]}'
```
Arjun (SE): telemetry queries to put in dashboards (example):
- median_latency_ms over 5m
- p95_latency_ms over 5m
- tokens_per_minute by tenant
- prefill_success_rate (prefill_success / prefill_attempts)
- fallback_rate (fallback_count / total_requests)
- active_warm_workers count
Priya (CS Ops): renewal followup cadence suggestion: day 7 check-in, day 14 product review + feature ask, day 21 risk triage if usage down.
WarmupBot: prefill job pf_45291 started for tenant T-ACME (requested by Arjun).
Nina (CSM): this feels customer-ready. Arjun/ Priya, please make a single-slide PDF and a short email template for AE to send. add the dashboard links and the three auto-check rules above.
Arjun (SE): will upload PDF and template to the shared drive within 45 minutes.
Leah (AE): thanks team 1 will schedule the 15m warmup after I get the PDF. :rocket:
